title: Restore the provision_vcs_auth self-heal for a bare Azure DevOps TF401019 G-push failure
description:
packages/apra-fleet-se/test/mock-sprint-member-vcs-provider-threading.test.mjs fails on its own assertion at line 107: "expected a provision_vcs_auth self-heal call for member 'local', got: []". This reproduces in fast replay/mock mode with NO real bd needed:

    cd packages/apra-fleet-se && node --test test/mock-sprint-member-vcs-provider-threading.test.mjs

(~560ms, ERR_TEST_FAILURE, same message as under real bd). The test file is unchanged since the de48e98c integration merge, so the production path moved, not the test.

Observed runtime behaviour on feat/azure-devops-vcs-auth: a bare TF401019 G-push failure is retried 3 times and surfaced as PostDispatchSyncError (code POST_DISPATCH_SYNC_FAILED, details.syncAttempts 3), cause GitSyncError (code GIT_SYNC_FAILED) thrown from syncMemberAfter (fleet-sprint/runner.js:937) via syncMemberAfterOrdered (runner.js:1105) via withGitSync (runner.js:6627 and 6642) -- but createVcsAuthSelfHealCallback never fires, so the harness's vcsAuthCalls array stays empty.

Likely cause: one of the Azure DevOps classification/seam commits on this track (07e64037, bd358e65, a6ffc58c, 8951bd56) changed how classifyGitFailure(text, provider) or the member provider resolution feeds the self-heal decision, so a bare TF401019 no longer classifies 'auth' at the point the self-heal branch is taken.

Done when: the mock-mode run above passes, the real-bd run of the same file passes, and a regression assertion pins that a bare TF401019 (no generic git-auth tail) on a per-member G-push triggers exactly one provision_vcs_auth self-heal for that member.

DIAGNOSIS (planner, re-plan 2026-08-20, reproduced on the current tree in replay mode, 0.5s, no real bd): classification and provider threading are NOT the defect. The sprint log already carries "auth git failure for member 'local' (G-push for 'local'); invoking self-heal (provision_vcs_auth) once" followed by "self-heal: auth failure detected for member 'local' ... calling provision_vcs_auth", so the bare TF401019 does classify as auth and the self-heal branch IS taken. What never happens is the actual tool call: the Azure DevOps provisioning argument builder (buildProvisionArgs in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/vcs-providers/azure-devops.mjs, around line 312) returns a typed error whenever no org can be derived from the member's git remote, and its caller (buildProvisionArgsForProvider in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js, around line 2301, used by the provisioning path around line 2393) turns that into a short-circuit before provision_vcs_auth is dispatched. The observed line is "ERROR: cannot provision Azure DevOps auth for member 'local': no organization could be derived from the member's git remote". That short-circuit is the residual mechanism - do NOT re-fix classifyGitFailure or the member provider resolution, both of which the same log proves are working. The earlier "likely cause" paragraph above is superseded by this diagnosis; keep it only as history.

FILES (pinned): packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/vcs-providers/azure-devops.mjs and packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js. In runner.js restrict yourself to the self-heal / provisioning region around buildProvisionArgsForProvider; the publish path further down the same file is owned by a different lane this sprint, so do not touch it. Decide deliberately whether a member whose remote yields no org should still reach provision_vcs_auth (letting the server produce the authoritative error) or whether the short-circuit is right and the missing self-heal call is instead a preflight-path expectation; either way the actionable operator message must survive and no secret value may be logged.

LANE: this task is the LAST member of the provider-descriptor lane, which owns every edit to packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/vcs-providers/*.mjs this sprint. The pull request builders, the provider-owned response mapping and the self-heal remedy fields all land earlier in this same lane - rebase onto them rather than re-deriving or re-declaring descriptor fields. The narrow real-bd concurrency measurement on this same test file is a READ-ONLY measurement in another lane and no longer gates this fix; if it has not run yet when you land, that is fine, it does not edit the file.

title: Azure DevOps auth failure classification and actionable remedies
description: Design slice C5 of apra-fleet-5co8. Today only a bare TF401019 is classified (AUTH_DENIED) and that verdict must stay as-is - an existing real-bd test asserts it end to end through withGitSync. Additive rules only, in the Azure DevOps provider module only: REST 401 and TF400813 mean an expired or revoked PAT (AUTH_EXPIRED); 403 permission refusals mean a missing-scope PAT (AUTH_DENIED with the scope-table remedy). The self-heal messaging for a PAT-family provider must state that server-side re-minting is impossible, unlike the GitHub App path.
acceptance_criteria: Expired/revoked PAT classifies AUTH_EXPIRED and surfaces the create-a-new-PAT plus credential_store_set plus re-provision remedy verbatim. Missing-scope PAT classifies AUTH_DENIED and cites the role/scope table in the Azure DevOps auth skill doc. Bare TF401019 still classifies AUTH_DENIED and toGitVerdict still collapses both to auth for legacy callers. Every new rule ships with its own test; no shared file gains a provider conditional.

Lane ado-classify uses 4-6 and runs after lane ado-foundation (1-3), because it edits the same Azure DevOps provider module.

title: Unattended Azure DevOps re-provisioning without an interactive prompt
description: Design slice C3 of apra-fleet-5co8. Sprint preflight and auth self-heal call provision_vcs_auth with only provider/git_access/repos, which for azure-devops triggers a blocking out-of-band prompt mid-sprint and then fails on a missing org_url. Add a buildProvisionArgs descriptor hook so the Azure DevOps module derives org_url from the members own remote and passes the PAT as a secure placeholder; secret name defaults to the documented convention and is overridable per sprint. Remote members have no secret store: placeholders resolve hub-side and the plaintext reaches a member only inside the executed command, so prefer stdin or encoded payloads over bare argv.
acceptance_criteria: An unattended sprint on an Azure DevOps member re-provisions with a derived org_url and a secure PAT placeholder and NEVER opens an out-of-band prompt. A missing secret produces a typed ERROR naming the remedial credential_store_set command. The raw PAT never appears in runner logs, prompts or transcripts. No if/switch on provider outside the provider module.

title: Azure DevOps remote-URL parsing and host recognition via provider descriptor hooks
description: Design slices C1 and C2 of apra-fleet-5co8. The fleet-sprint runner remote-URL parser only understands host/owner/repo, so an Azure DevOps remote parses to null and VCS auth preflight fails outright. Add an optional parseRepoRef(url) hook plus matchesHost/capabilitiesForHost to the vcs-providers descriptor shape, implemented in the Azure DevOps provider module only, dispatched via resolveVcsProviderForHost. OWNERSHIP: this feature owns C1+C2; the PR/comment builders (C4) are owned by the Azure DevOps create-pull-request builder bead - do not implement parseRepoRef twice.
acceptance_criteria: An Azure DevOps https remote (including a URL-encoded project name), the ssh v3 form, and a legacy visualstudio.com host all resolve to org/project/repo through the provider hook; a non-Azure remote keeps todays parse unchanged; an unparseable Azure remote yields a typed preflight ERROR naming the expected URL shape instead of an unexplained failure. Zero provider conditionals outside the provider module. Unit tests cover every URL shape.

title: Make the apra-fleet-se real-bd suite runnable from a scratch pre-fix checkout
description:
Verifying a before/after claim on the real-bd lane currently has no working recipe. `git worktree add <dir> <old-sha>` produces a tree whose apra-fleet-se tests fail immediately with:

    Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '@apralabs/apra-fleet-workflow' imported from packages/apra-fleet-se/test/helpers/mock-sprint-harness.mjs

because the npm workspace symlinks live only in the primary checkout's root node_modules. Symlinking the primary root node_modules into the worktree does not work on Windows Git Bash: `ln -s <primary>/node_modules <wt>/node_modules` resolves into the existing directory as node_modules/node_modules, and the @apralabs dir observable from the worktree contains only apra-fleet-client.

Deliver a documented, cross-platform recipe (and/or a small script) for standing up a pre-fix tree that can run `node scripts/run-tests.mjs real <files...>`, e.g. a scratch clone plus `npm ci`, or an explicit worktree bootstrap step. Add it to the integ test playbook so future timeout/perf beads can satisfy a 'reproduces on the pre-fix commit' criterion instead of reporting it as a blocker.

title: Azure DevOps PAT lifetime: expiry capture, propagation and real connectivity verification
description: Design slices C6, C7 and J1 of apra-fleet-5co8. DECIDED: a fleet holding only a PAT cannot self-extend it (the Azure DevOps PAT lifecycle API authenticates with an Entra OAuth token, not a PAT). Policy: optionally capture the PAT expiry at registration, propagate the resolved credential expiresAt into deploy metadata so the existing vcsTokenExpiresAt / checkVcsTokenExpiry / scheduleCredentialCleanup plumbing works, and add a day-scale warning threshold alongside the existing ten-minute one (which was designed for hour-lived GitHub App tokens). Reactive AUTH_EXPIRED classification is the backstop. Also replace the Azure DevOps connectivity stub, which curls the org root unauthenticated and verifies nothing.
acceptance_criteria: provision_vcs_auth on azure-devops propagates a supplied expiry into the member registry and emits a day-scale proactive warning when the PAT is near expiry; absent an expiry, nothing regresses and reactive classification remains the backstop. Connectivity verification exercises the deployed credential helper via git ls-remote against a concretely derived repo, with a documented clean skip when no repo is known, and never puts a raw PAT in a command. The onboarding doc states the secret-name convention and the optional expiry capture step.

title: [impl] Consume the provider-owned pull request response mapping in the publish path
description: LANE SEQUENCING: this lane (ado-pr-publish) runs after the Azure DevOps builder lane (ado-pr-a) completes - that lane defines the response-mapping contract this task consumes. PREREQUISITE: the provider descriptors must already declare their pull request response mapping (id field plus web URL template); if they do not, stop and report rather than implementing the mapping here. File: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js ONLY (the publish path around line 2601, which today hardcodes provider github in the buildCreatePrCommand call and reads html_url directly). Resolve the provider from the member/remote and read the pull request id and URL through the descriptor mapping instead of either dialect being known to the runner. The canonical contract mirror in src/services/vcs/types.ts and packages/apra-fleet-client is deliberately NOT part of this task - it is owned by the credential-descriptor lane (ado-debranch) so that shared contract file is edited from exactly one lane.
acceptance_criteria: Publish opens a pull request on a dev.azure.com remote and reports the correct id and web URL; GitHub publish output is byte-identical to today; runner.js no longer hardcodes a provider name at the publish call site and reads no provider-specific response field; runner.js is the only file this task changes.

title: [impl] Extend the interpret contract with provider-owned PR response-field mapping
description: Files: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/vcs-providers/index.mjs (document the contract), vcs-providers/azure-devops.mjs (declare idField pullRequestId and the web URL template built from org/project/repo and the id) and vcs-providers/github.mjs (declare its existing number and html_url mapping explicitly instead of leaving it implicit). Azure DevOps returns pullRequestId and no web URL field, so the mapping must be provider-owned rather than the runner knowing about either dialect. KB: no entry covers this contract - unexplored, premium tier.
acceptance_criteria: Both providers declare their response mapping in the descriptor; a canned Azure DevOps 201 body maps to the pull request id and a constructed web URL; a canned GitHub 201 body maps exactly as today; the contract is documented in index.mjs.

title: [test] Azure DevOps builder golden tests: exact command, redaction, and interpret contract
description: Add golden tests under packages/apra-fleet-se/test asserting the exact curl command produced for create-pull-request and comment (POSIX and Windows quoting), that logSafeCommand carries the redaction marker and that NO field other than command contains the token, and the interpret outcomes for 201, a generic 500, and 409 with TF401179. Also assert the capabilities table now reports canOpenPullRequest true for dev.azure.com and unchanged values for other hosts. No network.
acceptance_criteria: Tests pass and fail if the token leaks into a log-safe field, if the endpoint/api-version or ref shapes drift, or if the already-exists mapping is removed.

title: [impl] Implement Azure DevOps create-pull-request and comment builders and enable the PR capability
description: File: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/vcs-providers/azure-devops.mjs. Replace builders: null with create-pull-request and comment. create-pull-request POSTs to the org/project repository pullrequests REST endpoint at api-version 7.1 with sourceRefName and targetRefName as full refs/heads/ values plus title and description; auth is Basic with an EMPTY username (curl -u colon-token), the token appears ONLY in command and logSafeCommand carries the fixed redaction marker instead. interpret: success on 200-299; already-exists on 409 carrying TF401179. comment POSTs to the pull request threads endpoint with a single text comment and active status. Flip capabilitiesForHost canOpenPullRequest to true in THIS change so publish never builds an unsupported command. Use the shared quoting/token helpers, not copies. Permission note from the bead: PR creation is raw curl via execute_command, so the same Bash curl host grant that authorizes the GitHub REST calls must be mirrored for dev.azure.com (and vssps.dev.azure.com) - verify which runbook/bounds file grants the GitHub calls and add the matching entry. KB: no knowledge-bank entry covers these builders - unexplored, premium tier.
acceptance_criteria: buildVcsCommand for provider azure-devops returns a well-formed curl command for both actions; logSafeCommand contains the redaction marker and no token, and no other returned field carries the token; interpret maps 200-299 to success and 409 plus TF401179 to already-exists; capabilities for a dev.azure.com host report canOpenPullRequest true; unsupported actions still fail closed with the typed ERROR.

title: [impl] Hoist the shell-quoting and token-assertion helpers into a shared vcs-providers module
description: Files: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/vcs-providers/github.mjs and a new shared helper module next to it (plus the import line in any consumer). Move shQuote() and assertToken() out of github.mjs into the shared helper and import them back - a pure move, no behaviour change, so the Windows versus POSIX quoting rules stay identical for every provider rather than being copy-pasted for Azure DevOps. ASCII only.
acceptance_criteria: github.mjs imports both helpers from the shared module and defines neither; existing github builder tests pass unchanged; the helper is importable by other provider modules.

title: [test] Narrow concurrency repro proving the mock sprint file finishes inside the per-file timeout
description:
Do NOT verify by running the whole real-bd suite: that lane has a per-file budget problem of its own and is out of scope for this sprint. Use a NARROW repro instead: run this file (packages/apra-fleet-se/test/mock-sprint-member-vcs-provider-threading.test.mjs) concurrently with about 4 to 8 other bd-touching mock-sprint files against real bd (APRA_FLEET_BD_MOCK=0, concurrency 8), the same shape of repro apra-fleet-u87n.1 used, and capture every file's duration. Record the exact command and the measured durations in the close note so the result is reproducible.

ENVIRONMENT PROBE (planner, 2026-08-20, current tree): real bd DOES run here - packages/apra-fleet-se has no local node_modules but the root workspace hoist is sufficient, and this file completes standalone against real bd in about 26s (down from the ~89s standalone / 180000ms-under-concurrency figures on the bug). The earlier note that the P0 node_modules carry-over makes real bd unrunnable no longer matches the tree; if you hit an environment blocker anyway, record the exact command and its verbatim output.

BASELINE IS INHERITED, NOT RE-DERIVED: do NOT check out a pre-fix commit. apra-fleet-u87n.1's close note already records the before/after evidence (this file 160.0s -> 132.5s; sibling mock-sprint-publish-push-failure 180004ms FAIL -> 145.6s PASS; lane 21 pass/1 fail -> 22 pass/0 fail). Cite those numbers as the baseline and compare your fresh measurements against them.

KNOWN-RED, NOT YOURS TO FIX: on the current tree this file's LAST assertion fails - "expected a provision_vcs_auth self-heal call for member 'local', got: []" (test file line 107 region, the check after the three TF401019 classification checks). It fails in replay mode too (0.47s, no real bd involved), so it is a functional defect unrelated to real-bd contention and is OUT OF SCOPE for this task. Do not fix it, do not change the assertion; record the failure verbatim in the close note. The failing check runs AFTER runDevelopLoopScenario() returns, so the file's full bd-spawn workload still executes and its wall-clock duration remains a valid measurement of the contention property this task gates on.

The already-committed packages/apra-fleet-se/test/bd-replay-read-cache.test.mjs (commit de32ad62) pins the bd-replay read-cache invalidation behaviour in replay mode; it is useful but it does NOT satisfy this task, which requires a real-bd concurrent timing measurement.

LANE (re-plan 2026-08-20): this task is a READ-ONLY measurement - it runs the file and records durations, it does not edit it - so it no longer shares a lane with the functional fix for the known-red assertion. That fix may therefore land before or after this measurement. If the last assertion is already GREEN when you run, record that verbatim instead and treat it as expected, not as a discrepancy; the duration measurement this task gates on is unaffected either way.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A narrow concurrent real-bd repro is documented in the close note: the exact command, the file list (this file plus about 4 to 8 other bd-touching mock-sprint files), the concurrency setting, and the per-file wall-clock durations.
2) TIMING GATE: every file in that lane completes without hitting the 180000ms per-file timeout, and mock-sprint-member-vcs-provider-threading.test.mjs in particular finishes with clear headroom under it. Durations are compared in the close note against the baseline numbers inherited from apra-fleet-u87n.1's close note (no pre-fix-commit re-run).
3) CLASSIFICATION GATE: the file's three TF401019 checks still hold under that run - the persistent G-push surfaces as a sync error, an "auth git failure for member 'local'" log line is present, and no "unknown git failure for member 'local'" line appears. These are observable in the output even though the file reports FAIL overall.
4) CARVE-OUT: the file's final provision_vcs_auth self-heal check ("expected a provision_vcs_auth self-heal call for member 'local', got: []") is known-red on this tree in replay mode as well, is not contention-related, and is NOT a pass/fail gate for this task. It must be recorded verbatim in the close note and left unfixed.
5) The sibling carry-over mock-sprint-publish-push-failure.test.mjs is included in the lane and its duration recorded, but its result is NOT a gate for this task.
6) If real bd genuinely cannot be run, the close note reports the blocker with the exact command executed and its verbatim failure output - a bare assertion that the environment is broken does not satisfy this task.
7) WORKLOAD SANITY: record the number of real bd spawns this file makes during the measured run and compare it to the 27 spawns (about 47.6s of exec time) recorded in apra-fleet-u87n.1's close note. If the count is materially lower, say so explicitly and state that the missing provision_vcs_auth self-heal plus its bounded retry reduced the workload, so the measured duration is a floor rather than a like-for-like comparison against the 132.5s baseline. A fast run that is fast because work was SKIPPED does not satisfy the timing gate.
